comparisons.peer_topic: Estimate Range of Possible Loss and Uncertainties
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, the estimated range of possible loss for disclosed matters is $0 to $0.8 billion in excess of any accrued liability. These estimates are based on currently available information and significant judgment, with actual losses potentially varying significantly due to unpredictable nature and uncertainties.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America disclose the aggregate range of reasonably possible unaccrued losses for legal and regulatory matters as of December 31, 2024. Citigroup estimates this range to be up to approximately $1.3 billion, whereas Bank of America's estimate is lower, ranging from $0 to $0.8 billion. Both disclosures emphasize that these estimates involve significant judgment and uncertainty, with Bank of America explicitly noting the estimates are based on currently available information and subject to significant judgment.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024, Citigroup estimates that the reasonably possible unaccrued loss for these matters ranges up to approximately $1.3 billion in the aggregate.

For any matter disclosed in this Note for which a loss in future periods is reasonably possible and estimable (whether in excess of an accrued liability or where there is no accrued liability), the Corporation's estimated range of possible loss is $0 to $0.8 billion in excess of the accrued liability, if any, as of December 31, 2024.

The accrued liability and estimated range of possible loss are based upon currently available information and subject to significant judgment, a variety of assumptions and known and unknown uncertainties.

comparisons.peer_topic: Legal Proceedings Estimation Methodology and Liability
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm is involved in various judicial and regulatory proceedings, many in early stages with indeterminate damages. For estimable matters, the upper end of the reasonably possible loss range is estimated at approximately $1.7 billion in excess of aggregate reserves as of the filing date.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Citigroup both provide an aggregate estimate of the upper end of the reasonably possible loss range for legal matters where a loss is estimable. As of the end of 2024, Citigroup estimates the unaccrued loss to be up to approximately $1.3 billion, while Goldman Sachs estimates the upper end of the range to be approximately $1.7 billion in excess of aggregate reserves. Both disclosures identify these figures as applying to matters where management is able to form an estimate, distinguishing them from matters with indeterminate or unestimable exposures.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024, Citigroup estimates that the reasonably possible unaccrued loss for these matters ranges up to approximately $1.3 billion in the aggregate.
Many of these proceedings are in early stages, and many of these cases seek an indeterminate amount of damages.

Under ASC 450, an event is "reasonably possible" if "the chance of the future event or events occurring is more than remote but less than likely" and an event is "remote" if "the chance of the future event or events occurring is slight." Thus, references to the upper end of the range of reasonably possible loss for cases in which the firm is able to estimate a range of reasonably possible loss mean the upper end of the range of loss for cases for which the firm believes the risk of loss is more than slight.

comparisons.peer_topic: Litigation Reserve Policy and Aggregate Estimated Losses
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, the Firm estimates the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses for legal proceedings to be $0 to approximately $1.4 billion, noting that estimates involve significant judgment due to the number, stages, and uncertainty of proceedings. The Firm accrues litigation liabilities under U.S. GAAP when probable and estimable, adjusting quarterly based on counsel consultation, having incurred $740 million in legal expenses in 2024, though future adjustments are not assured given the difficulty in predicting outcomes.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup both disclose the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses for legal proceedings in excess of established reserves for the 2024 fiscal year. JPMorgan estimates a range of $0 to approximately $1.4 billion, while Citigroup estimates the unaccrued loss ranges up to approximately $1.3 billion. Both firms highlight that these estimates involve significant judgment and that actual losses may vary significantly from these estimates due to the inherent uncertainties of litigation.

In addition, while many estimates presented in financial statements and other financial disclosures involve significant judgment and may be subject to significant uncertainty, estimates of the range of reasonably possible loss arising from litigation, regulatory and tax proceedings are subject to particular uncertainties.

The Firm believes the estimate of the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses, in excess of reserves established, for its legal proceedings is from $0 to approximately $1.4 billion at December 31, 2024.
The Firm's estimate of the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses involves significant judgment, given:
Accordingly, the Firm's estimate of the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses will change from time to time, and actual losses may vary significantly.

comparisons.peer_topic: Difficulty in estimating legal loss contingencies
comparisons.peer_summary: It is often difficult to determine if a loss is probable or reasonably possible, or to estimate the amount, particularly when factual records are contested, damages are substantial or indeterminate, or novel legal questions arise.
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup and Morgan Stanley both address the challenges and uncertainties inherent in estimating loss contingencies for legal proceedings. Citigroup notes that estimates of reasonably possible loss are subject to particular uncertainties (S003), while Morgan Stanley elaborates that it is inherently difficult to determine if a loss is probable or to estimate the amount, particularly when factual records are contested or damages are substantial. While Citigroup provides a specific aggregate estimate ($1.3 billion), Morgan Stanley's cited text focuses on the qualitative difficulty of estimation rather than providing a specific aggregate figure in the same context.

sentences.text: In addition, while many estimates presented in financial statements and other financial disclosures involve significant judgment and may be subject to significant uncertainty, estimates of the range of reasonably possible loss arising from litigation, regulatory and tax proceedings are subject to particular uncertainties.
In many legal proceedings and investigations, it is inherently difficult to determine whether any loss is probable or reasonably possible, or to estimate the amount of any loss.

It is particularly difficult to determine if a loss is probable or reasonably possible, or to estimate the amount of loss, where the factual record is being developed or contested or where plaintiffs or government entities seek substantial or indeterminate damages, restitution, forfeiture, disgorgement or penalties.
